questions.stem: The simplest hydrocarbon, found as the main component of natural gas, is:
questions.explanation: Methane (CH₄) is the first member of the alkane series and makes up 70-95 % of natural gas and biogas. It is also a potent greenhouse gas — about 25 times more effective per molecule than CO₂ over 100 years. Ethane (C₂H₆), propane (C₃H₈), butane (C₄H₁₀) are the next members; LPG is mainly a mix of propane and butane.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The functional group —OH is characteristic of which class of organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Alcohols carry the hydroxyl (—OH) group attached to a saturated carbon. Examples: methanol CH₃OH, ethanol CH₃CH₂OH. Aldehydes have —CHO (e.g., formaldehyde HCHO); carboxylic acids have —COOH (acetic acid CH₃COOH); esters have —COO-R (ethyl ethanoate). Phenols also have —OH but attached to an aromatic ring.

questions.stem: The alcohol present in alcoholic beverages such as beer and wine is:
questions.explanation: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) — produced by the yeast fermentation of sugars (glucose, fructose) — is the drinkable alcohol in beer (4-8 %), wine (10-14 %) and spirits (40 %+). Methanol (CH₃OH) is highly toxic — causes blindness and death even in small doses; illicit 'hooch' poisoning cases are methanol contamination. Glycerol is a triol used as a sweetener and humectant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Benzene, a common aromatic hydrocarbon, has the molecular formula:
questions.explanation: Benzene — C₆H₆ — is a flat hexagonal ring with alternating single and double bonds (or better, delocalised π-electrons over the ring). It was first proposed in this structure by Kekulé. C₆H₁₂ is cyclohexane (saturated); C₆H₁₄ is hexane (straight-chain saturated); CH₄ is methane. Benzene is a known carcinogen; exposure from petrol fumes is tightly regulated.

questions.stem: The polymer used to make plastic bottles, packaging films and beverage containers (known as PET) is:
questions.explanation: PET — polyethylene terephthalate — used in nearly all disposable water and cola bottles, carries the '1' recycling code. Polyethylene (PE — codes 2, 4) is used for plastic bags and HDPE containers. PVC (code 3) is used for pipes and window frames. Polystyrene (code 6) is used for thermocol and disposable cups.

questions.stem: The building blocks (monomers) of proteins are:
questions.explanation: Proteins are long chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Twenty amino acids make up almost all natural proteins. Nine are 'essential' — the body cannot synthesise them and must obtain them from food. Fatty acids build lipids; nucleotides build nucleic acids (DNA, RNA); monosaccharides like glucose and fructose build carbohydrates.

questions.stem: Acetic acid, the main acid in vinegar, has the chemical formula:
questions.explanation: Acetic acid (ethanoic acid) is CH₃COOH — a 2-carbon carboxylic acid. Vinegar is typically 4-8 % acetic acid. HCOOH is formic acid, found in ant stings. C₂H₅OH is ethanol. C₆H₈O₇ is citric acid, the main acid in lemons.
